title: Coronary autoregulation: local metabolites (nitric oxide + adenosine)
vignette: Researchers are observing how coronary blood flow changes in response to progressive increases in the mean arterial blood pressure. On the graph of coronary blood flow versus perfusion pressure, there is a mostly horizontal (flat) portion indicating a region where coronary blood flow is relatively insensitive to blood pressure changes. Within this zone of autoregulation, the metabolic demands of the myocardium are the main determinant of coronary blood flow. Which of the following endogenous factors is most responsible for controlling coronary blood flow within this range?

clues.text: mostly horizontal (flat) portion indicating a region where coronary blood flow is relatively insensitive to blood pressure changes
clues.note: A flat pressure-flow curve is the autoregulatory zone, where local (metabolic) mechanisms keep flow nearly constant despite changing perfusion pressure.

clues.text: metabolic demands of the myocardium are the main determinant of coronary blood flow
clues.note: In the autoregulatory range, LOCAL metabolic factors (adenosine and nitric oxide) - not systemic pressure - set coronary blood flow to match myocardial oxygen demand.

whatMatters: Within the autoregulatory zone, coronary blood flow is matched to MYOCARDIAL OXYGEN DEMAND by locally released vasodilator metabolites - chiefly ADENOSINE and NITRIC OXIDE. Of the choices, NITRIC OXIDE (endothelium-derived) is the key endogenous controller. Answer D.
strategy: Recall coronary autoregulation: the myocardium extracts ~70% of oxygen at rest, so increased demand must be met by increased FLOW, controlled locally by ADENOSINE (from ATP breakdown) and NITRIC OXIDE (endothelial). Pick nitric oxide. Reject autonomic/systemic vasoactive agents that have minor roles in autoregulation: acetylcholine (vasodilates via NO but minor), angiotensin II and norepinephrine (vasoconstrictors, systemic), histamine and serotonin (variable, not autoregulatory).

eliminations.label: Acetylcholine - vasodilates via NO but minor autonomic role
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: acetylcholine causes coronary vasodilation by stimulating endothelial nitric oxide release. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: autonomic input has a relatively small effect on coronary flow compared with locally released metabolites; NITRIC OXIDE (the effector) is the better answer. ✅ Correct if: asking about parasympathetic/endothelial-dependent vasodilation.

eliminations.label: Angiotensin II - vasoconstrictor, not autoregulation (your pick)
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: a systemic vasoconstrictor (RAAS). ❌ WHY IT FAILS: it constricts coronary arteries and is not part of local coronary autoregulation. ✅ Correct if: systemic vasoconstriction/blood-pressure regulation.

eliminations.label: Histamine - variable, not autoregulatory
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: histamine has variable vasoconstrictor/vasodilator effects depending on receptor. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: it does not play a significant role in coronary autoregulation. ✅ Correct if: an inflammatory/allergic vascular response.

eliminations.label: Norepinephrine - vasoconstrictor (alpha-1)
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: causes coronary vasoconstriction via alpha-1 receptors. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: autonomic sympathetic tone has a small effect versus local metabolites, and it constricts rather than autoregulates flow. ✅ Correct if: alpha-1-mediated vasoconstriction.

eliminations.label: Serotonin - GI/CNS, coronary vasospasm (not autoregulation)
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: serotonin (mainly GI/CNS) can cause coronary vasospasm (5-HT1 agonists like triptans). ❌ WHY IT FAILS: it is not significantly involved in coronary autoregulation. ✅ Correct if: triptan-associated coronary vasospasm.

reasoning: The flat portion of the coronary pressure-flow curve is the autoregulatory zone (flow matched to demand, not pressure)
The myocardium extracts most available oxygen at rest, so demand is met by adjusting FLOW via local vasodilators
Local control is dominated by adenosine and NITRIC OXIDE
mechanism: The myocardium has the highest resting oxygen extraction of any tissue (~70% of delivered oxygen at baseline, versus ~30% elsewhere), so an increase in myocardial oxygen demand can only be met by a corresponding INCREASE IN CORONARY BLOOD FLOW. CORONARY AUTOREGULATION keeps flow relatively constant (the flat region of the pressure-flow curve, ~60-140 mm Hg) by adjusting vascular resistance according to metabolic need. This is accomplished mainly by LOCALLY acting vasodilators: ADENOSINE (released from cardiomyocytes as ATP is consumed for energy) and NITRIC OXIDE (synthesized by endothelial cells in response to shear stress and chemical mediators). When perfusion pressure falls (or demand rises), reduced oxygen delivery increases adenosine and nitric oxide, which relax vascular smooth muscle and dilate the coronaries to restore/maintain flow; the reverse occurs when pressure rises. Of the listed choices, NITRIC OXIDE is the key endogenous controller. Autonomic mediators (acetylcholine, norepinephrine) have comparatively small effects on coronary flow, angiotensin II and (variably) histamine/serotonin are vasoconstrictive or unrelated to autoregulation.

difficulty.label: 🧠 Knowledge
difficulty.text: First Aid CV/Physio > coronary autoregulation: high resting O2 extraction; local metabolites adenosine + nitric oxide match flow to myocardial O2 demand (flat pressure-flow curve, ~60-140 mm Hg); autonomic input minor.

difficulty.label: 📖 Comprehension
difficulty.text: Autoregulation is driven by local vasodilators - adenosine and nitric oxide - not systemic pressor agents.

difficulty.label: 🔤 Vocab
difficulty.text: Unsure on autoregulation, oxygen extraction, adenosine, nitric oxide, or pressure-flow curve? Tell me which.

difficulty.label: 🨤 Distractor
difficulty.text: Angiotensin II/norepinephrine constrict; acetylcholine (via NO) and histamine/serotonin play minor/variable roles - NO is the local effector.

difficulty.label: 🖼️ Imaging / diagram
difficulty.text: On the graph: the flat middle portion (coronary blood flow constant across a range of perfusion pressures) is the autoregulatory zone controlled by local metabolites. Anchor: 'flat pressure-flow curve = local control = adenosine + nitric oxide.'

difficulty.label: 🗒️ Other
difficulty.text: Bank: coronary autoregulation = adenosine + nitric oxide match flow to O2 demand; myocardium extracts ~70% O2 at rest.

Physio > heart extracts ~70% at rest -> flow-dependent.

memoryHook: The heart already grabs almost all the oxygen it can, so when it needs more it must open the pipes - local adenosine and nitric oxide crank up flow, indifferent to the systemic pressure.
